text: One morning the Monarchs arrived to find Miss Churm and Oronte already posing together, and the Major, standing in silence, seemed to understand at last what their presence in my studio meant. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, remarking that the girls hair might be better done, Missus Monarch went over to Miss Churm and, with a few quick touches, made her head twice as charming as before. <break time="0.8s" /> It was a small act, but it was the service of a ladys maid, not of a lady, and seeing it, I felt something tighten in my throat that I could not quite name. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, while I worked, the Major and his wife quietly washed up my crockery and put it away, and Missus Monarch picked up a dirty rag that had dropped from my paint box. <break time="0.8s" /> I say, can I not be useful here, the Major asked at last, and in that question I heard what they could not bring themselves to say aloud, Take us on, and we will do anything. <break time="0.8s" /> They had accepted their failure, but they could not accept their fate, and for a moment, as I watched them, my drawing blurred before my eyes and the whole picture swam. <break time="0.8s" /> I kept them for a week, but it was a pity I could not bear, and at last I gave them a sum of money to go away, and I never saw them again. <break time="0.8s" /> Hawley still insists that the Monarchs did me a permanent harm and led me into false ways, and if that be true, I am content to have paid the price, for the memory.
